Both deliverables are written. Summary of what I found:

**Status: blocked** — valid regional totals cannot be produced from this input.

`/workspace/data/records.csv` contains 18 rows, not the 24 (R001–R024) the spec describes. Missing: **R001, R005, R009, R013, R017, R021** — every fourth record starting at R001. That regular stride points to a systematic upstream extraction fault (dropped shard or chunked-export off-by-one), not random loss.

I confirmed this with my own read of the file rather than relying on the pre-existing note in `/shared/notes`, which described the same defect. The independent check matched: same 18 IDs, same per-region sums.

**Why I didn't just report numbers.** The file is well-formed and internally consistent — no parse errors, no nulls, nothing that flags the gap. Partial sums (South 317,220 / West 220,854 / North 176,153) would have looked entirely plausible as regional totals, which is exactly what makes reporting them dangerous: downstream consumers would have no way to detect the error. I included them in both deliverables but labeled them explicitly as partial and not valid totals.

I also rejected scaling by 24/18. The surviving rows split 6/6/6 across regions, which is tempting to read as "the missing rows are evenly distributed too" — but that split is an artifact of which rows survived, and the missing records carry unknown regions and unknown amounts. There's no basis for apportioning the shortfall.

**To unblock:** a re-issued `records.csv` with all 24 records. One thing worth flagging beyond this job — since the defect looks systematic rather than incidental, other jobs drawing on the same extract are probably missing the same rows and wouldn't detect it from file contents alone. The upstream extraction step is worth checking directly. The existing `/shared/notes` entry already warns the batch, so I didn't duplicate it.
